assessments.technical_explanation: The workflow has no explicit permissions block. For pull_request events from forks, GitHub defaults to read-only token permissions, and this workflow only checks out code and runs local node scripts without needing write access. The absence of an explicit permissions declaration is a best-practice gap, not an exploitable over-grant in this context.
assessments.layman_explanation: The CI workflow does not spell out what permissions it needs. In practice GitHub gives it only read access for pull requests, which is all this workflow uses, so there is no real danger—just a missing best-practice line.
assessments.developer_action: Add an explicit permissions block with contents: read to the job or workflow.

assessments.technical_explanation: The setup-node action is pinned to the v4 major-version tag rather than a full commit SHA. This is widespread practice for first-party GitHub actions, but SHA pinning is the recommended hardening against tag-retag supply-chain attacks. The workflow runs on pull requests, so a compromised action could execute in CI context, but the blast radius is limited to the CI runner with read-only token scope.
assessments.layman_explanation: The workflow uses a version label for a build tool instead of locking it to an exact code snapshot. If that label were ever hijacked, the CI could run altered code, but this is a low-probability event for official GitHub-provided tools.
assessments.developer_action: Pin actions/setup-node to a full commit SHA for supply-chain hardening.

assessments.technical_explanation: The checkout action is pinned to the v4 major-version tag rather than a full commit SHA. Same supply-chain consideration as the setup-node step. The workflow does not upload artifacts or expose secrets beyond the default read-only token, limiting impact.
assessments.layman_explanation: The workflow uses a version label for the code-checkout tool instead of an exact snapshot. This is a minor hardening gap with low real-world risk for an official GitHub action.
assessments.developer_action: Pin actions/checkout to a full commit SHA for supply-chain hardening.

assessments.technical_explanation: The artipacked pattern concerns credential persistence when workflow artifacts include the .git directory with an embedded token. This workflow never uploads artifacts; it only runs local node scripts and a git diff check. The checkout default persists a token in .git/config on the runner, but without artifact upload there is no exfiltration path.
assessments.layman_explanation: This finding is about secrets leaking through saved build artifacts. The workflow never saves any artifacts, so there is nothing for a secret to leak through.
